profile.campus: Equinix Los Angeles IBX campus
profile.reading:
This is Equinix's LA7 facility at 1501 Francisco Street in Torrance, California, part of Equinix's Los Angeles-area data center network, distinct from the company's much larger Silicon Valley cluster around San Jose and Santa Clara where Equinix was founded in 1998. Equinix's own published specifications describe LA7 as spanning 74,981 square feet, with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 5kVA, dual 120v/208v power distribution, generators providing 2/N+1 redundancy with 30 hours or more of autonomy at full load, N+20% cooling redundancy, aspirated fire detection, and a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, holding certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High. Equinix specifically markets LA7 as serving internet content delivery and entertainment companies worldwide, positioning the facility for increased performance and low latency to accelerate customer time-to-market, a framing that reflects Los Angeles's status as a major hub for the media and entertainment industry alongside its general role as a Pacific Rim network gateway. Equinix, which converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015 and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX, operates LA7 as part of a broader Los Angeles-area IBX network that, like its Silicon Valley and Northern Virginia counterparts, positions the company as a neutral interconnection point for competing networks rather than a single-tenant cloud campus. Equinix's LA7 page did not disclose a specific opening date for the Torrance facility in the material fetched this session.

Southern California Edison, the regional utility serving Torrance, has cited data center and other large commercial load growth in its own long-range distribution planning, and Los Angeles County's status as a major submarine-cable landing point for trans-Pacific network routes has made LA-area interconnection facilities like LA7 increasingly important to content and entertainment companies routing traffic to and from Asia-Pacific markets.

profile.reading:
This building is Equinix's SV3 facility, part of Equinix's Silicon Valley data center network in the San Jose/Santa Clara area. Equinix was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson, both former Digital Equipment Corporation facilities managers, on the idea of building a neutral place where competing internet networks could physically connect and exchange traffic, a model that let the company grow through network effects as more networks joined; Equinix converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015 and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX. Silicon Valley, where Equinix is still headquartered today in nearby Redwood City, was the company's founding market, and its San Jose facilities on Great Oaks Boulevard and its Santa Clara facilities on Corvin Drive and Duane Avenue grew into one of the densest interconnection hubs in Equinix's global network as the company expanded internationally, entering Asia-Pacific in 2002, Europe via the IXEurope acquisition in 2007, Latin America in 2011, and the Middle East in 2013, and opening its 50th global data center in London by 2010 around the time it acquired Switch and Data Facilities Company. Equinix's own published specifications for the flagship SV1 building on this campus describe an 82,850-square-foot, single-story, steel-frame facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 2kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, and generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load; Equinix markets the Great Oaks campus for its direct connections to major networks and tier-1 cloud service providers. Equinix's website did not disclose this specific building's own square footage or power capacity separately from the SV1 figure cited as representative of the broader campus.

Pacific Gas and Electric, the regional utility serving most of Silicon Valley, and Silicon Valley Power, Santa Clara's municipal utility, have both cited sustained data center load growth across the San Jose-Santa Clara-Sunnyvale corridor in their own capacity planning, a dynamic distinct from the newer data center markets elsewhere in the country given how built-out and power-constrained the Bay Area grid already is after decades of continuous data center development since Equinix's own 1998 founding in the area.

The building functions as a major hub for Latin American and Caribbean connectivity given Miami's position as a subsea cable landing point, and its hurricane-category-5 engineering and elevated siting reflect its role as critical infrastructure for a hurricane-prone metro. Equinix's current MI1 property page (added as a second source alongside the Wikipedia entry) confirms the building remains an active, named facility within Equinix's Miami-metro colocation portfolio, though it does not itself disclose current occupied sqft or MW figures separate from the Wikipedia-sourced 750,000 sq ft total.

Miami-Dade County's data center market has grown substantially since Equinix's 2016-2017 acquisition of this building, with the county now hosting one of the densest concentrations of subsea cable landing stations in the Western Hemisphere; the NAP of the Americas name persists in industry and local usage even though Equinix has marketed the building as MI1 since taking ownership, and it remains one of the largest single data center buildings by square footage documented anywhere in this registry.

This Secaucus/North Bergen cluster sits in Hudson County, New Jersey, roughly 10 miles from Lower Manhattan; the area's lower real estate costs and proximity to the Wall Street financial corridor, rather than any single anchor tenant, are what have concentrated Equinix's largest East Coast metro campus here rather than in New York City itself.

profile.campus: Warsaw (Salomea district), Poland (Equinix WA3)
profile.reading:
This is Equinix's WA3 facility at Aleje Jerozolimskie 213 in the Salomea district of Warsaw, Poland; this row carried no operator website URL on file until a same-day research pass located Equinix's dedicated WA3 page by matching the URL pattern already on file for sibling Italy and Finland rows, substituting Poland's country and region path segments. That page describes WA3 as a three-story, reinforced-concrete building with 1,400 square meters, about 15,069 square feet, of colocation space, N+1 power and cooling redundancy, generator autonomy of 30 hours or more at full load, and a 99.9999%-plus global uptime guarantee, though it does not publish a specific IT capacity figure in megawatts or kilowatts. Equinix entered the European colocation market through its 2007 acquisition of IXEurope and expanded further through its 2015 acquisition of TelecityGroup for about $3.8 billion, though Equinix's current WA3 page does not attribute the building to either predecessor company by name. Equinix, founded in Silicon Valley in 1998, converted to a real estate investment trust in January 2015 and trades on Nasdaq as EQIX; the company's own about page states a current global footprint of 281 data centers across six continents, while Wikipedia separately cites approximately 260 data centers across 33 countries as of 2025.

As an EU-based facility, this data center falls under the European Union's Energy Efficiency Directive reporting requirements, which since 2024 have required data centers above a minimum capacity threshold to report power usage effectiveness, water usage, and other sustainability metrics to a European Commission database, part of a broader EU push for standardized data center energy transparency that does not have a direct equivalent in most of the US markets covered elsewhere in this registry.

profile.campus: Dallas, Dallas County, Texas (Equinix Infomart campus)
profile.reading:
Per Equinix's own site (its DA1 Dallas building page) and Wikipedia's entry on the Infomart building, the Infomart housing multiple Equinix Dallas suites is located at 1950 North Stemmons Freeway, Dallas, TX 75207. The building opened in 1985 as part of Trammell Crow's Dallas Market Center on the former P.C. Cobb Stadium site, an $85 million, Crystal-Palace-inspired structure spanning 1,583,309 sq ft across 7 floors and 18.2 acres, one of Dallas's largest buildings, with over 8,700 strands of fiber optic cabling and more than 135 network providers maintaining a physical presence, and five independent electric feeds to three separate electrical substations. ASB Real Estate Investments bought the property in the early 2000s; Equinix acquired it in April 2018 for $800 million and now operates four International Business Exchange (IBX) data centers within it, DA1, DA2, DA3 and DA6, serving over 530 customers including Google Cloud Platform and Microsoft Azure, alongside other colocation operators (DataBank, Cologix, Flexential) and non-data-center tenants (Wade College) that also occupy space in the shared building. In 2020 Equinix announced a $142 million expansion including a new data center and a 5G proof-of-concept center within the campus, and by 2025-2026 the company had filed to develop an additional two-building DA12 campus nearby at 1550 West Mockingbird Lane on a former printing-company site, a roughly $836 million combined investment across DA12-1 and DA12-2. This registry entry represents the shared Infomart building broadly rather than one specific numbered Equinix suite, so no single-suite sqft or MW figure is asserted for it individually; the address and building-level facts above are confirmed.

Texas's absence of a state corporate income tax and its status as a major fiber crossroads between the coasts have helped make Dallas one of Equinix's largest US metros by facility count; the Infomart's scale and shared-tenant model, with multiple competing colocation operators inside one historic building, is unusual within Equinix's portfolio, which more typically favors company-owned, single-operator IBX buildings like the newer DA12 campus now under development nearby.

profile.reading: This building is Equinix's DC1 facility on Equinix's Ashburn, Virginia campus, part of what Data Center Dynamics has called the birthplace of the commercial internet: AOL built the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support dial-up internet operations, and the fiber infrastructure that project attracted helped trigger the region's growth into Data Center Alley in Loudoun County, now described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix established its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and DC2, which followed, has been described by Data Center Dynamics as reputedly the most connected building on earth; Equinix's own published specifications for DC2 describe a single-story, reinforced-concrete, 118,446-square-foot facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High. Equinix has continued expanding the Ashburn campus well beyond DC1 and DC2, eventually building out numbered facilities into the twenties as demand grew, with Data Center Frontier reporting on Equinix's plans for a fleet of four-story buildings as part of that expansion. Equinix positions the Ashburn campus as serving one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, offering colocation in private cages, smart-hands support, managed solutions, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and its own Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products. Equinix's own website confirms this building's address and IBX facility code but, consistent with the rest of Equinix's public site, does not publish this specific building's power capacity or square footage beyond the DC2 example cited above as representative of the campus's general specifications.

profile.campus: Culpeper, Virginia (former Terremark government-focused campus, acquired by Equinix 2016; Culpeper Technology Zone)
profile.address: 18155 Technology Drive, Building B, Culpeper, VA 22701
profile.reading: This is Equinix's CU2 facility at 18155 Technology Drive, Building B, in Culpeper, Virginia, part of a former Terremark campus that Equinix acquired in 2016. Data Center Dynamics reported the campus was originally developed in 2008 to serve government customers, spans roughly 60 megawatts across multiple buildings, and sits within the Culpeper Technology Zone, a deliberately managed development area the county has kept to avoid sprawl. Equinix's own published specifications for CU2 describe a two-story, precast-concrete-and-steel-frame building of 62,398 square feet, with N+1 power redundancy, N+2 generator redundancy providing 30 hours or more of backup at full load, 24/7 security including biometric-entrance mantraps, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, and SOC 2 Type II; Equinix markets CU2 specifically as offering "secure, government-grade capacity" with a hardened design for compliance-driven infrastructure, a positioning DCD linked to the area's history serving federal customers. Culpeper's data center growth is closely tied to Cold War-era federal infrastructure: the nearby Mount Pony bunker, a Federal Reserve communications and records facility from the 1960s through the late 1990s, later became the Library of Congress's National Audio-Visual Conservation Center rather than a data center, but the area's existing power and security infrastructure it attracted helped seed early data center activity, including a Swift financial-network data center dating to the 1980s that DCD reported still operates today. DCD quoted an industry analyst describing Culpeper as "proving a fairly friendly area for data centers," citing abundant developable land, dual utility service from both Dominion Energy and Rappahannock Electric Cooperative, and its position roughly 55 miles south of the established Ashburn hub as a growth corridor positioned as complementary to, rather than competing with, Loudoun County.

profile.campus: Seattle, King County, Washington (Equinix SE2/SE3, adjacent to the Westin Building)
profile.reading:
Per Equinix own site, this SE3 facility is located at 2020 Fifth Avenue, Seattle, WA 98121 and totals 36,457 sq ft. Redundancy: N+1 Cooling redundancy. No MW power capacity figure is published on this page.

Per Data Center Knowledge's coverage of its opening, SE3 was converted from a six-story parking garage adjacent to the Westin Building (home to Equinix's original SE2 facility) and opened in March 2013; the conversion, a 50-50 joint development between Digital Realty Trust and Clise Properties, added roughly 51,000 sq ft with capacity for more than 1,000 cabinets and 4.1 megawatts of IT capacity across four floors, with direct connectivity to the Seattle Internet Exchange (SIX) and round-the-clock operations and security. Its proximity to SE2 in the Westin Building lets customers with existing deployments expand within the same connected campus rather than establishing a new interconnection point elsewhere in the metro.

Washington state's relatively low-cost hydroelectric power and absence of a state income tax have made it an attractive secondary market for colocation operators expanding beyond Seattle's core Westin Building carrier hotel; SE3 and SE2 together anchor Equinix's Pacific Northwest interconnection point, giving customers direct cross-connects to the subsea cable systems that land in the region and link to Asia-Pacific markets.

Equinix's Seattle metro page positions SE2, SE3 and the Kent, WA-based SE4 together as serving 4,900+ enterprises with connectivity reaching more than 60% of the Fortune 500 globally; SE3's conversion from a parking structure rather than ground-up construction mirrors a pattern seen elsewhere in Equinix's portfolio (including at some Ashburn, Virginia and Northern California sites) where the company has adapted existing urban structures to add capacity quickly in supply-constrained downtown submarkets rather than waiting for greenfield development.
